subject: Operational buffer proposal and monthly credit mechanics for SLA
messages:
From: Danielle Park <danielle@cumuluspay.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.ai
Cc: contracts@cumuluspay.com
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA follow-up — monthly credit mechanics

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the call this morning. CumulusPay's legal team flagged the proposed monthly credit matrix as hard to reconcile with our intermittent peak traffic pattern — we asked whether Redwood would consider a small ‘operational buffer’ before credits kick in, and a clearer pro‑rata formula for partial-month incidents.

From our side we'd like:
- A 0.25% monthly buffer (i.e., credits only apply to uptime below 99.75%)
- A simple pro‑rata calculation when an incident spans multiple billing cycles
- Explicit callouts about maintenance windows and whether scheduled infra upgrades count toward the buffer

Can you run this by your procurement/legal and get back with language we can take to our counsel? We're aiming to finalize by the end of next week.

Best,
Danielle
Director, Platform Ops
CumulusPay

Attachments: contract-markup-v3.pdf (stated)
From: irene.choi@redwood.ai
To: Danielle Park <danielle@cumuluspay.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA follow-up — monthly credit mechanics

Danielle —

Appreciate the clear asks. Karthik and Ben looped in for procurement/offer-side language. Quick proposal we drafted internally (attached PDF and XLS):

High-level summary:
- Operational Buffer: a one-time monthly buffer of 0.20% (credits apply for uptime below 99.80%). We suggest 0.20% rather than 0.25% to balance your tolerance and our uniform template.
- Credit Bands: soft band (99.80–99.50) — 5% of monthly invoice; hard band (below 99.50) — escalated sliding scale up to a 50% monthly credit. Exact figures in XLS.
- Pro‑rata for cross-cycle incidents: credit is applied pro‑rata to the billing period(s) based on incident overlap hours. Example in the XLS: a 36‑hour incident crossing months results in a weighted credit across both invoices.
- Maintenance carveouts: scheduled maintenance (72‑hour rolling notice for major infra work; 24 hours for minor) is excluded from uptime calculations. Emergency maintenance will be evaluated case-by-case; if issued during our defined maintenance window no credit applies.
- Latency SLOs: separate metric. We propose p95 <= 350ms for API response time; failure to meet latency SLOs triggers a non‑monetary remediation plan plus tiered credits only if p95 breaches persist for 3 consecutive days.

Next steps: Ben — can you pull a concise redline of the SLA paragraph language (2–3 bullets) we can send to Danielle's counsel? Karthik — confirm whether the buffer should be 0.20% or 0.25% from a commercial perspective.

Thanks,
Irene
Head of Customer Contracts | Redwood Inference

Attachments: 20270615-sla-operational-buffer-draft.pdf, CumulusPay-MAP-v2.xlsx
From: ben.carter@redwood.ai
To: irene.choi@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 12:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA follow-up — monthly credit mechanics

Irene — quick redline below for Danielle's counsel. I kept the language tight so their legal team can substitute.

Proposed SLA paragraph (redline-ready):
- For the purpose of monthly uptime calculation, an Operational Buffer of 0.20% (the Buffer) will be applied to the total available service time for each calendar month. Credits will be computed only for the portion of downtime that exceeds the Buffer.
- Credit Bands: If monthly uptime (after Buffer) is between 99.50% and 99.80%, Customer is eligible for a credit equal to 5% of the monthly service fee. If monthly uptime (after Buffer) is below 99.50%, Customer is eligible for credits on a sliding scale up to 50% of the monthly service fee as set forth in the Service Credits table.
- Pro‑rata: If an incident spans two or more billing periods, the Service Credit will be allocated to each affected billing period based on incident hours falling within that period.
- Maintenance: Scheduled maintenance announced according to the Maintenance Policy will be excluded; emergency maintenance will be reviewed and excluded only where documented evidence supports operational necessity.

Commercial note: We can accept 0.25% buffer if they ask, but we should increase the top-end credit by 5 percentage points to compensate (i.e., scale max credit to 55%). I recommend holding 0.20% initially.

Ben
VP, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Danielle Park <danielle@cumuluspay.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.ai
Cc: contracts@cumuluspay.com
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA follow-up — monthly credit mechanics

Irene / Ben —

Thanks — that language is straightforward and our counsel liked the pro‑rata example in the XLS. Two quick asks before we loop legal for redlines:
1) Would Redwood accept the 0.25% buffer if we agree to a 12‑month commitment term (we're prepared to move to annual billing)?
2) Can we get a short carveout that clarifies Latency SLO credits are not monetary but trigger a remediation credit (e.g., a one‑time credit or account credit) if p95 > 600ms for 7 consecutive days?

If you can confirm those two points we'll send an in‑principle redline from counsel and schedule a signoff call.

—Danielle
Director, Platform Ops
CumulusPay
